The moving average convergence divergence (MACD) indicator is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price. The MACD line is the difference between the 12-day exponential moving average (EMA) and the 26-day EMA. The signal line is a 9-day EMA of the MACD line. When the MACD line crosses above the signal line, it is a buy signal. When the MACD line crosses below the signal line, it is a sell signal. The MACD indicator is currently above its signal line, but the signal line is pointing down. This indicates that the stock could be on the verge of a sell signal.

The relative strength index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in an asset. The RSI is calculated by dividing the average gain of prices over a specified period by the average loss of prices over the same period. The RSI is a bounded oscillator that ranges from 0 to 100. A reading above 70 indicates that the asset is overbought and a reading below 30 indicates that the asset is oversold. The RSI is currently at 33.26, which is below the neutral level of 50. This indicates that the stock is oversold and could be due for a rebound.

The Fibonacci retracement levels are a set of horizontal lines that are used to identify potential areas of support and resistance. The Fibonacci retracement levels are based on the Fibonacci sequence, which is a series of numbers where each number is the sum of the two previous numbers. The most common Fibonacci retracement levels are 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. The most recent Fibonacci retracement level is 23.6%, which is below the current price of the stock. This indicates that the stock could have further to fall before it finds support.
